title: Binance Says BTC, ETH, XRP and 7 Other Cryptos Fully Backed After Hack
summary: Binance said 10 cryptocurrencies were fully backed after replenishing 90% of stolen assets. The exchange is sourcing less liquid tokens to close the remaining shortfall while targeting a Sunday withdrawal restart. 10 Cryptos Fully Backed as Binance Narrows Shortfall Binance reported progress replaci...
content:
Binance said 10 cryptocurrencies were fully backed after replenishing 90% of stolen assets. The exchange is sourcing less liquid tokens to close the remaining shortfall while targeting a Sunday withdrawal restart.

Key Takeaways

  • Less liquid tokens account for the outstanding 10% of stolen assets.
  • Company funds and emergency reserves support the replenishment effort.
  • Withdrawals remain targeted for Sunday, Nov. 1, Binance said.

10 Cryptos Fully Backed as Binance Narrows Shortfall

Binance reported progress replacing stolen assets in its third security incident update on X on Oct. 31. After noting that approximately 80% of the hacked losses had been covered at the time of its preceding update, the exchange stated:

“That covered amount is now up to 90%. All BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC are fully backed 100%.”

Less liquid cryptocurrencies outside that group make up the remaining shortfall, and industry partners are helping source sufficient quantities. More than $6.34 billion in company funds had been set aside under the preceding recovery plan.

“We will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and OTC channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens. Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users,” the crypto exchange pledged.

The exchange’s initial hack findings pointed to a possible compromised employee laptop that enabled unauthorized withdrawal submissions. Binance reported no evidence of leaked wallet private keys at that stage. Its original loss-coverage pledge named SAFU and company funds.

Emergency and Insurance Funds Support Token Purchases

Replenishment draws on corporate treasury funds, futures insurance reserves, and the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency reserve protecting user assets during security incidents. A partial SAFU deployment was expected within 24 hours of the statement, with its public bitcoin wallet available for monitoring. Binance committed to restoring SAFU to approximately $1 billion.

The fund’s conversion from stablecoins into bitcoin began earlier this year, including a first $100 million batch reported in February. Its broader allocation plan targeted $1 billion in BTC. Despite bitcoin already being fully covered, part of SAFU would finance purchases of other outstanding tokens.

Futures Insurance Funds cover deficits from bankrupt trading positions and help pay profitable positions in full. Addressing their use, Binance stated:

“Binance has rebalanced its Futures Insurance Funds to move a portion of the balance to cover the affected assets.”

The company said it released only excess reserves, leaving the required regulatory balance and internal risk coverage intact.

Those reserves include liquidation clearance fees, charges imposed when positions are forcibly closed, and receive company top-ups when required. Binance monitors historical stress scenarios but acknowledged that volatility can trigger auto-deleveraging, which automatically reduces other traders’ profitable positions when insurance reserves cannot absorb bankrupt positions. The publicly available fund balance refreshes daily at midnight Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Reserve Verification Pending as Sunday Restart Target Holds

A new snapshot taken at midnight UTC on Oct. 31 was published through Binance’s proof-of-reserves system, the exchange said. Generating the zero-knowledge proof, which verifies calculations without exposing individual customer balances, requires approximately 40 to 50 hours. Holders of the 10 tokens were expected to be able to verify minimum 1:1 backing by Tuesday, Nov. 3, UTC.

Customer verification checks account inclusion in Binance’s liabilities calculation, while public blockchain transaction records show address holdings and transfers. The futures insurance fund is tracked separately as company reserves and is outside customer proof of reserves.

Resuming withdrawals remained Binance’s next operational milestone. In its Oct. 31 statement, the exchange said it remained on track to reopen withdrawals Sunday, Nov. 1. It planned to provide another update once the reopening details were confirmed.

title: Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance
summary:
Key Takeaways: On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks. Eighteen years later, Bitcoin
The post Bitcoin Whitepaper Turns 18: How Satoshi’s 9-Page Vision Reshaped Global Finance appe...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • On October 31, 2008, the Bitcoin whitepaper was published by Satoshi Nakamoto, which outlines a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, without the need for banks.
  • Eighteen years later, Bitcoin developed from a novel monetary system to an asset owned by public organizations, investment funds, and governments.
  • Bitcoin Archive celebrated the occasion on its X page, restating the bold conclusion that the crypto industry began.

Bitcoin’s whitepaper was created on October 31st, 2008, marking 18 years in digital asset history. The initial allotment of nine pages of documents to send the funds without any process of money brokering has now become a worldwide network of trillions of dollars’ worth.

  • Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money
  • Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community
    • The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Satoshi Nakamoto Introduced a Different Way to Move Money

On October 31, 2008, an individual or group using the name Satoshi Nakamoto published Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System on a cryptography mailing list.

One major problem with online payments was that too often, financial institutions had to confirm the transfers of funds and avoid double spending. Satoshi envisioned a new peer-to-peer system that did not require central control to function: When people make an exchange, the transaction is verified using cryptographic proof, with a shared and publicly visible record containing the transactions.

This design was a distributed ledger plus proof-of-work. The miners confirm transactions, create new blocks, and miners are rewarded with transactions whenever the network follows the longest chain with largest proof-of-work.

On January 3, 2009, the Bitcoin network came into operation by mining the first block. This protocol later comes to be associated with a maximum supply of 21 million BTC and the assets are issued at a predictable time frame.

Read More: Michael Saylor Teases More Bitcoin After Strategy’s $69.45B Reserve Hits 848,250 BTC

Bitcoin Has Moved Beyond Its Early Cypherpunk Community

The network has since expanded well beyond the realm of cryptography, where the paper first appeared. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024, providing another channel for traditional investors to buy Bitcoin without owning cryptocurrency wallets.

Public companies are also including Bitcoin on their balance sheets. Some other examples include strategy being the largest publicly listed corporate holder and the U.S. government creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve in March 2025 using seized Bitcoins.

This represents a significant shift from Bitcoin’s early years, when every Bitcoin was dominated by technology enthusiasts and early adopters.

The 18th Anniversary Brings Attention Back to Satoshi’s Idea

Bitcoin Archive recently marked the occasion on X with a message celebrating 18 years of Bitcoin and thanking Satoshi Nakamoto. Another aspect of the network’s creation was also touched on in the post, the historic moment.

18 years of Bitcoin.

Thank you, Satoshi — what an incredible journey. https://t.co/DhYNB3SZ9y

— Bitcoin Archive (@BitcoinArchive) October 31, 2026

However, Bitcoin’s original concept has stayed true to its nature, allowing users to make transactions on a public network without a bank or payment company approving it.

Satoshi’s identity remains unknown, and the white paper’s publication began a project that would eventually influence thousands of other digital assets and blockchain networks.

title: Binance says 90% of stolen assets replenished, targets Sunday withdrawals
summary: Less-liquid tokens make up the remaining shortfall as Binance continues buying replacement assets through market and over-the-counter trades.
content:
Binance said Saturday it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in its $6.3 billion hack, up from 80% a day earlier, and remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday.

The exchange is using a combination of its corporate treasury, a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and a portion of its futures insurance fund, a spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

“Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not users,” the spokesperson said, adding that the insurance fund would remain above required risk management levels.

The update follows Thursday’s theft, the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, which TRM Labs has since attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacker group.

Following the hack, Binance said Friday it had set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses, including $5 billion in the affected cryptocurrencies. Industry partners like Tether and Circle froze about $3 billion in affected assets after the hack, but those funds are separate from Binance’s replacement of stolen tokens.

Still, CertiK told Cointelegraph on Friday that it needed more information to verify Binance’s claimed $5 billion in replacement cryptocurrencies. Binance has since published a new reserves snapshot, but says the full cryptographic proof is still being generated. “The full zero-knowledge proof takes approximately 40 to 50 hours to generate due to the computational workload,” the exchange’s update reads.

Binance said in its update on X that customer balances in Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and eight other assets were fully backed. The remaining shortfall consists of less liquid tokens that it continues to buy through market and over-the-counter transactions, the update reads.

The spokesperson’s statement did not specify how much each funding source contributed or disclose the insurance fund’s minimum required balance. It also did not quantify how much stolen crypto had been recovered.

Read Cointelegraph’s full coverage of the Binance hack here.

Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

title: Bitcoin held up better than expected after Binance hack, Strive CEO says
summary: Strive CEO Matt Cole says the Binance hack has not changed his long-term case for Bitcoin, but cautions it is too early to call a market bottom.
content:
Bitcoin has held up better than expected following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to Strive CEO Matt Cole, who said the breach does not undermine the cryptocurrency’s long-term investment thesis.

Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction on Friday, Cole said the breach had not changed his long-term investment case for Bitcoin. He compared the attack on Binance’s wallets to a bank robbery rather than a failure of Bitcoin’s network.

Bitcoin traded near $77,400 at 4:00 pm on Saturday, about 4% below its price shortly before the attack began Thursday, according to CoinGecko data.

Strive, a publicly traded company that holds Bitcoin on its balance sheet, reported owning 43,000 BTC as of Oct. 23.

“I do have conviction that over any reasonable time frame, this does not change the investment thesis on Bitcoin,” Cole said.

Cole said Bitcoin’s decline was less severe than he expected given the scale of the breach and broader market weakness, although he acknowledged that it was too early to determine whether the cryptocurrency had reached a price bottom.

Cole described the market as being in an “early spring” recovery phase that could last another six to nine months, with prices gradually rising rather than surging to new highs.

Paul Chapman, financial crime director at Wirex, also distinguished the attack on Binance from a compromise of Bitcoin’s network. “It’s important to be clear that Bitcoin itself hasn’t been hacked — this was an attack on one company’s systems, not the network,” he told Cointelegraph.

Related: Strive closes $630M SATS IPO, leaves Bitcoin allocation unspecified

Bitcoin reaction compared with Bybit

According to Glassnode, Thursday’s Binance breach was the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, with around $6.3 billion affected, exceeding the combined losses from the next nine largest hacks. The previous record was the $1.5 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025.

Glassnode said three of the 10 largest crypto hacks have occurred since the beginning of 2025, all involving exchanges.

Binance hack exceeds the next nine largest crypto exploits combined. Source: Glassnode

By comparison, following the Bybit hack in 2025, Bitcoin fell roughly 5% from nearly $100,000 to around $95,000 amid the breach and broader market volatility, according to a Bitfinex market report.

Anchorage Digital data cited by CNBC put Bitcoin’s average decline in the first 24 hours after previous crypto exchange exploits at 8.3%.

Binance hack exposes exchange security vulnerabilities

Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan said the attackers appeared to have compromised Binance’s transaction signing process. Binance said Friday that it had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys, though its investigation remained ongoing.

Blockaid’s analysis identified an Ethereum transaction containing 50 signed authorizations covering different transaction counts. A matching authorization allowed attacker-controlled code to operate through the wallet. Ben-Natan argued that checks before signing could have blocked the malicious authorization.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto: Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations. Coinbase led a selloff in crypto-linked stocks following Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack, and Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses from the attack.

Binance hack sparks pre-election political clashes 

Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations.

President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied.

The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss.

It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3 billion Binance hack

Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.

Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.

The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.

The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

Binance says it holds $5 billion in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Binance said Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from its hack, with $5 billion already in held in the same tokens stolen.

“The $5 billion is held in the exact token assets that are required. These assets are in Binance custody,” a Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.

The spokesperson declined to disclose the wallet addresses, citing security reasons, but said that the holdings would appear in the exchange’s next proof-of-reserves report, which shows the assets it holds to back customer balances.

Binance said it provides weekly reports on its company funds to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market in the United Arab Emirates. The exchange said the requirement predated the hack.

title: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?
summary: In typical Bitcoin style, the number one cryptocurrency turns 18 today, amid AI-driven security threats, quantum fears and the biggest exchange hack in crypto history.
content:
Eighteen years ago today, pseudonymous cypherpunk Satoshi Nakamoto posted the Bitcoin whitepaper, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, to a cryptography mailing list.

Created to bypass opaque institutions and remove the need for trust in financial transactions, Bitcoin (BTC) has been taking on the traditional financial system since its genesis block was mined on Jan. 3, 2009.

Inscribed in that very first block was a message from Satoshi, quoting a headline from The Times: “Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.” It captured the financial crisis backdrop against which Bitcoin was born.

From its early years to adulthood, Bitcoin has had a tumultuous journey, fraught with controversy, intrigue and downright skulduggery.

As challenging as the journey has been, Bitcoin’s future remains on fragile ground, with the fallout from the $6.3 billion Binance hack, the threat of quantum computing, the acceleration of AI-related cyber threats, and questions over its long-term security still looming.

As Bitcoin celebrates its 18th birthday, it’s now old enough to vote in the US midterm elections, but is it ready for adulthood?

Bitcoin’s early years

Undoubtedly, one of Bitcoin’s most memorable moments was on May 22, 2010 when developer Laszlo Hanyecz sent 10,000 BTC to pay for two pizzas in one of the earliest documented Bitcoin transactions.

The Bitcoin Whitepaper. Source: Bitcoin.org

The day would become known as Bitcoin Pizza Day and go down in crypto folklore as the most expensive pizza purchase on record. The coins were worth around $41 at the time, taking the concept of opportunity cost to a whole new high — those pizzas would have cost $780 million at today’s prices.

Related: 10 of the greatest unsolved crypto mysteries

Bitcoin traded for pennies in its earliest days, but Satoshi understood how that would change one day, writing in 2009, “It might make sense just to get some in case it catches on.”

By late 2013, Bitcoin had broken through the $1,000 milestone for the first time, amid growing public interest with the emergence of the Silk Road darknet marketplace.

Yet nowhere do the laws of physics apply more pertinently than crypto; inevitably, what goes up must come down. In February 2014, Bitcoin’s epic run came to an abrupt end when Mt. Gox, the world’s largest Bitcoin exchange at the time, suddenly stopped trading and went offline.

The exchange had lost around 850,000 BTC, including customers’ funds, in a collapse that sent shockwaves through the industry, making Mt. Gox an early poster child for the concept “not your keys, not your coins.”

Craig Wright, Jamie Dimon and China’s first ban

The next dramatic bull run would culminate in Bitcoin’s price climbing from below $1,000 at the beginning of 2017 to almost $20,000 by December.

The rally coincided with a boom in initial coin offerings (ICOs) and a rush of projects promising to use blockchain technology for everything from banking to supply chains, and even Long Island iced tea.

Suddenly, every man, woman and dog wanted a blockchain, even if they had no idea how Bitcoin worked or where it came from.

Everyone, that is, except JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, who called Bitcoin “a fraud” in September 2017 and said he would fire any employee trading it.

Bitcoin genesis block. Source: Mempool.space

At the time, Bitcoin was embroiled in a bitter debate over how the network should scale. The so-called “block size war” peaked in August 2017, culminating in the hard fork that created Bitcoin Cash and highlighting the complications of trying to change a decentralized system.

Related: Private, fast USDT is coming to Bitcoin. Can it compete with Ethereum and Tron?

Meanwhile, China moved against the industry, banning ICOs in September 2017, taking action against cryptocurrency exchanges and fanning the market uncertainty ahead of the eventual downturn in 2018.

Speculation over the identity of Bitcoin’s creator had also become a sideshow, fueled by Australian computer scientist Craig Wright’s repeated claims to be Satoshi Nakamoto. The UK High Court rejected his claim in 2024.

China’s second ban and the collapse of FTX

Bitcoin’s next major bull run came during the COVID-19 pandemic, as governments and central banks unleashed a tsunami of money printing in a bid to cushion economies from lockdowns.

Interest rates fell, liquidity flooded financial markets and Bitcoin, which had plunged during the March 2020 market panic, began a remarkable recovery, reaching almost $69,000 by November 2021.

As if China’s intervention wasn’t enough the first time around, Beijing stepped in again to rain on the parade, announcing a sweeping ban on cryptocurrency transactions and mining in September 2021, and Bitcoin’s price took a hit.

In November 2022, another major cryptocurrency exchange, FTX, collapsed, intensifying the crypto winter and leaving customers facing enormous losses.

The episode led to a loss of trust from the TradFi sector and a spate of regulatory hostility toward crypto, in what the industry would dub “Operation Chokepoint 2.0.” Bitcoin’s downward spiral was once again painful and steep.

The first Bitcoin ETF and $100,000

Just when sentiment in the industry was circling the drain, a silver lining appeared in January 2024 from one of the unlikeliest sources. The US Securities and Exchange Commission, which had repeatedly rejected spot Bitcoin product applications, approved the first US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products.

The SEC approved a US spot Bitcoin ETF. Source: SEC.gov

The nod from the SEC finally gave investors a regulated route to gain exposure to BTC without having to manage wallets or private keys themselves. At the end of that year, Bitcoin’s price broke through $100,000 for the first time.

Related: Bitcoin ETF inflows climb to $176M as BTC rebounds above $80K

Since then, traditional finance has continued to move closer to crypto, with banks moving into custody and trading services and heavyweights like BlackRock CEO Larry Fink talking about putting everything from stocks to bonds on the blockchain.

Even Dimon shifted his stance from outright dismissal to allowing clients to buy the asset. The original cryptocurrency went on to hit a new all-time high of more than $126,000 in October 2025.

Bitcoin’s all grown up, but what about the future?

Bitcoin is firmly in the embrace of TradFi once again, with some sizable regulatory tailwinds from Washington and abroad.

The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation in US Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act has established a federal framework for stablecoins, the SEC has offered greater clarity on how securities laws apply to crypto assets, and Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) has given the local industry a more harmonized regulatory framework.

Yet the institutionalization of the space has led many Bitcoiners to question whether institutions holding so much BTC are concentrating ownership and centralizing supply — and indeed whether the cypherpunk movement has been captured by the very institutions it sought to rebel against.

There are bigger questions looming over Bitcoin’s long-term security, too, including the threat of quantum computing, which many fear could break the cryptography that secures Bitcoin.

A proposed upgrade known as BIP-360 outlines a new type of Bitcoin output to reduce certain quantum vulnerabilities, but as the community learned from the block size war, the challenge will be agreeing on any new implementation before the threat arrives.

And quantum computing is not the only security question Bitcoin needs to resolve. This week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, the largest crypto exchange hack on record, has renewed fears about the security of centralized exchanges, the stability of crypto infrastructure and the potential for further market turmoil.

There’s also the question of who pays to keep the network secure as the block subsidy trends to zero, and whether transaction fees alone will be enough to compensate the miners securing the network.

Transaction fees accounted for just 0.67% of total miner revenue in the 90 days to Oct. 4 and have remained below 5% of miner revenue for most of Bitcoin’s history. That leaves a huge gap for fees to fill as block rewards diminish with each halving.

Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin

Bitcoin has endured more than your average teen as it comes of age, surviving exchange collapses, regulatory crackdowns, civil wars and repeated market crashes.

It has also become something Satoshi may not have foreseen: an asset held by Wall Street and traded through mainstream financial products.

title: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) Price Prediction: Can Bulls Break $0.011 Resistance and Trigger a Major Rally?
summary: Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is facing another important test as traders monitor whether buyers can regain control after a prolonged decline.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: PENGU

Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) is facing another important test as traders monitor whether buyers can regain control after a prolonged decline.

PENGU recently traded near $0.0073, with technical analysts identifying $0.011 as a critical resistance level that has repeatedly limited recovery attempts.

Despite occasional rebounds, PENGU remains under pressure across several timeframes. Traders are watching nearby support around $0.0070 and $0.0068, while a deeper historical support zone near $0.0055 could become important if selling resumes. The latest chart analysis suggests that a sustained move above resistance could improve the outlook, although current indicators do not yet confirm a broader bullish reversal.

PENGU Price Faces Key Resistance Near $0.011

Crypto trader @MstrTranquility recently highlighted PENGU’s daily chart, identifying approximately $0.011 as a persistent resistance zone. According to the analyst’s technical assessment, the token has faced repeated rejections around this level over several months.

The chart highlights resistance near $0.011 and support around $0.0055, with a potential sharp rally if resistance is breached. Source: @MstrTranquility via X

The chart also identifies approximately $0.0055 as an important support area, where buyers have previously stepped in to defend the price. The distance between these two levels outlines a broad trading range that could determine PENGU’s next significant move.

A decisive breakout above $0.011 would indicate that buyers are overcoming a resistance zone that has repeatedly restricted upward momentum. However, a brief move above the level would not necessarily establish a lasting trend reversal. Sustained trading above resistance, supported by stronger volume, would provide more convincing evidence of improving demand.

Another trader, @alekstraderx, shared a 12-hour Bybit perpetual chart showing additional support and resistance confluence zones. The analysis places a nearby support area around $0.0068, with overhead resistance extending toward $0.0106.

These levels offer a more detailed view of PENGU’s shorter-term trading structure. The $0.0068 region is particularly relevant because it sits below the psychological $0.0070 threshold. A successful defense could help stabilize the token, while a sustained breakdown may expose it to additional selling pressure.

PENGU Technical Indicators Maintain a Bearish Bias

TradingView’s technical summary points to a difficult market structure for PENGU despite its occasional intraday recoveries. At the time of the supplied analysis, the token was trading around $0.00735, up approximately 0.88% over 24 hours.

However, the broader performance remained negative. PENGU had declined approximately 4.82% over seven days and 22.95% over the previous month. Its market capitalization stood near $464 million, reflecting the impact of the recent correction.

The 12-hour Bybit perpetual chart highlights key PENGU support near $0.0068 and resistance up to $0.0106 amid a prevailing downtrend. Source: @alekstraderx via X

Moving averages remain an important obstacle for a sustained recovery. Several short- and long-term simple moving averages (SMA) and exponential moving averages (EMA) were positioned above the spot price in the supplied technical assessment. This configuration suggests that previous support levels have turned into potential resistance zones.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) also provides limited evidence of an immediate reversal. Rather than showing an extreme oversold reading that might indicate an exhausted sell-off, the indicator remains closer to neutral or weaker momentum territory.

TradingView’s broader technical assessment therefore favors caution. A modest daily recovery does not necessarily mean that the prevailing downtrend has ended. Buyers would need to reclaim important moving averages and establish higher price lows before the market structure could be considered more constructive.

$0.0083 and $0.0070 Define the Immediate PENGU Price Outlook

In the shorter term, approximately $0.00829 represents an important overhead resistance level in the supplied TradingView analysis. Reclaiming this area could help PENGU move away from its immediate bearish structure and bring higher resistance zones into focus.

A sustained move above $0.0083 would provide an early indication that buying pressure is improving. However, the token would still need to overcome the broader resistance around $0.0106 to $0.011 before a stronger bullish scenario could develop.

Pudgy Penguins (PENGU) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

On the downside, $0.0070 represents an immediate psychological support level. Maintaining this area could allow the token to consolidate and attract buyers following its recent correction.

The nearby $0.0068 zone identified in the 12-hour Bybit chart provides another level to monitor. If PENGU loses both $0.0070 and $0.0068, selling pressure could increase as traders reassess the likelihood of a recovery.

A deeper support area near $0.0037 also appears in the TradingView assessment. This level represents a more distant downside reference rather than an immediate target. A move toward it would require a substantial deterioration in the current price structure.

Pudgy Penguins’ NFT Brand Provides Broader Market Context

PENGU is associated with the Pudgy Penguins ecosystem, which began as an Ethereum-based NFT collection of 8,888 individual penguin characters in 2021. The project subsequently expanded beyond digital collectibles into physical merchandise, including plush toys distributed through major retail channels.

This expansion has helped establish Pudgy Penguins as a consumer-facing Web3 brand rather than an NFT project focused exclusively on digital trading. Its physical products have also introduced the brand to audiences who may not actively participate in cryptocurrency markets.

The PENGU token has a maximum supply of approximately 88.89 billion tokens. Despite the brand’s broader commercial presence, the token remains exposed to cryptocurrency market volatility, speculative trading activity, and changing investor sentiment.

PENGU also trades substantially below its 2024 all-time high, which was approximately $0.068 according to the market data. Its current price near $0.0073 represents a significant decline from that historical peak.

The distinction between brand expansion and token performance remains important. Commercial visibility does not automatically translate into sustained demand for the associated cryptocurrency. Market participants will continue to assess token liquidity, trading activity, and broader market conditions when evaluating PENGU’s valuation.

Can PENGU Break $0.011 and Trigger a Major Rally?

The $0.011 resistance zone remains the central level in the bullish scenario for Pudgy Penguins. A successful breakout could signal a shift in market sentiment, particularly if it coincides with increasing trading volume and improving momentum indicators.

Before reaching that level, however, PENGU must overcome intermediate resistance around $0.0083 and the broader $0.0106 area. These price zones could attract sellers and limit recovery attempts. Buyers would need to establish sustained support above each threshold to strengthen the case for further upside.

The bearish scenario remains relevant if the token fails to hold its nearby support levels. A breakdown below $0.0068 could weaken the short-term structure, while a deeper decline toward $0.0055 would bring the historical support zone highlighted by @MstrTranquility back into focus.

For now, PENGU’s technical outlook remains cautious. Its expanding consumer brand offers a broader ecosystem narrative, but the price chart continues to reflect selling pressure. A confirmed breakout above $0.011, rather than an isolated upward move, would provide stronger evidence that bulls are regaining control.

title: Texas brothers sentenced to 15 years in prison for armed crypto robbery, kidnapping
summary: Home invasions became the most common form of crypto wrench attacks worldwide during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 incidents from one.
content:
Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced to 180 months and 186 months in prison, respectively, for their armed robbery of cryptocurrency and kidnapping of a family in Grant, Minnesota.

The brothers were sentenced on Thursday before US District Judge Donovan W. Frank, according to a Friday news release. They had pleaded guilty in June.

On Sept. 19, 2025, the brothers, who had traveled from Texas to Minnesota, kidnapped Victim 1 and his family in their home at gunpoint, court documents said. They zip‑tied the family at gunpoint and held them for more than nine hours, demanding access to Victim 1’s cryptocurrency accounts.

When the brothers did not receive the amount of cryptocurrency expected, they forced Victim 1 to drive to a cabin in upstate Minnesota, where they obtained additional cryptocurrency from other devices for a total of more than $8 million. 

The brothers fled after the victim’s son called 911, and police later identified and arrested them near Houston.

Brothers terrorized family at gunpoint

“Raymond and Isiah Garcia violated the sanctity of a home, abducted a victim, terrorized a family at gunpoint for hours, and disrupted an entire community in a brazen act of violence and greed,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson.

Cointelegraph reported in July that home invasions had become the most common form of crypto wrench attacks during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 publicly reported incidents from just one a year earlier, according to blockchain security firm CertiK. 

CertiK said in July it verified 52 wrench attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 33% from 39 incidents during the same period in 2025. Kidnappings rose to 16 from 12.

title: Binance $6.3B record hack sparks pre-election political clashes
summary: Some political and administration figures tried to make hay of the biggest-ever crypto heist.
content:
Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations.

President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied.

The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss.

It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

Wyoming Senator Cynthia Lummis, a Republican and longtime crypto advocate, cited the stalled Clarity Act in a Friday post on X. “Yesterday, hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in less than 4 hours, the biggest heist in history. The Clarity Act would have given crypto firms legal cover to freeze suspicious transactions the instant law enforcement calls. Every minute lost is money gone for good,” she wrote.

Related: FBI and Secret Service join response to Binance’s $6.3B hack

Clarity Act stalled over ethics provisions

The Senate on Sept. 15 failed to pass a cloture motion on the Clarity Act that would have established the country’s first regulatory framework for digital assets.

The bill had stalled over proposed ethics provisions that would restrict government officials and their families from issuing or profiting from digital assets while in office.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission then submitted a regulatory action on Sept. 18 covering crypto asset transactions and markets for White House review, as the agency moved forward with its approach to overseeing the digital asset sector.

CFTC Chair Michael Selig referred to crypto market regulation on Friday after the Binance hack, saying in a TV appearance: “This proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets. … The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States.”

Still, Democratic Representative Maxine Waters said in a Friday news release that “The reported $6.3 billion hack of Binance should be a wake-up call to anyone who thinks the cryptocurrency industry can operate without strong accountability. Yet, Trump and Congressional Republicans have been set on pushing a deregulatory agenda that weakens compliance mandates and oversight of the crypto industry, not to mention the Trump family’s own questionable ties to the company.”

Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded

Trump family and Binance

She also commented on past relations between Binance and the Trump family, saying, “Remember that after Binance’s owner, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), gave over $2 billion to the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial, Trump’s Securities and Exchange Commission’s Chair Paul Atkins dropped the SEC’s slam-dunk fraud case against Binance and CZ, and Trump fully pardoned CZ, allowing him to again get involved with crypto.”

Meanwhile, Binance said it was working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover the stolen funds.

The company also promised to publish a postmortem incident report after conducting a full security review.

“We will provide a detailed technical report outlining what happened, the lessons learned and the additional safeguards being implemented,” Binance said.

title: Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing
summary:
Key Takeaways: The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing. All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk. The
The post Bank of England Opens Tokenized Collateral Door With 2027 Deadline for UK Clearing appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Bank of England is seeking input on tokenized collateral for central clearing.
  • All tokenizable assets must be equally liquid and equally risky in terms of risk.
  • The consultation will be open until Feb. 12, 2027.

The Bank of England comes closer and closer to introducing tokenized assets into the mainstream of the UK market infrastructure.

The central bank has launched a consultation outlining how central counterparties, or CCPs, could accept tokenized versions of eligible collateral without creating a separate regulatory regime for blockchain-based assets.

  • Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral
  • Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome
    • Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later
    • UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

Bank of England Opens the Door to Tokenized Collateral

The proposal concentrates on assets that are or could be already collaterized according to the UK’s CCP.

The Bank says tokenization by itself won’t bar an asset from being accepted. What’s important is whether the collateral remains easily transferable and saleable, has little credit risk and market risk, and can still be valued.

The Bank has reported that tokenization of collateral can facilitate trades of assets across markets and jurisdictions, particularly in meeting margin calls. Faster collateral movement could also reduce operational friction in clearing and support wider adoption of digital market infrastructure.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

Same Risk, Same Regulatory Outcome

The Bank is sticking to a simple rule: tokenized collateral should achieve the same regulatory result as traditional collateral. That means CCPs would need to show that digital representations of assets remain accessible and transferable even during stressed market conditions.

The regulator additionally urges firms to look at the risk associated with technology, custody arrangements and reliance on third-party infrastructure. For instance, tokenized security relying on a bridge that links blockchain records to other asset locations would require knowledge of the consequences of the bridge being compromised.

Stablecoins Could Enter the Conversation Later

The consultation doesn’t instantly add to the list of collaterals that are eligible. It primarily concentrates on the tokenisation of assets currently allowed under the existing regulations, such as cash, financial instruments, bank guarantees and gold, provided they meet established criteria.

But also the Bank´s position is seeking input from industry on a wider array of assets that may qualify in the future. That conversation also covers tokenized money market fund shares, tokenized gold, and stablecoins, so it’s applicable to the entire crypto ecosystem.

Some digital assets could eventually comply with existing collateral standards, the Bank said, and advised firms contemplating digital assets to reach out to supervisors early on.

UK Pushes Tokenization Deeper Into Wholesale Finance

The consultation is part of a wider consultation by the Bank of England, Financial Conduct Authority and HM Treasury in the UK. Their mission is to establish a more straightforward rule for tokenized securities and settlement in the digital medium, while fostering financial stability.

It will help foster responsible tokenization while maintaining the resilience of financial market infrastructure, said Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, Sarah Breeden. The consultation will continue through Feb. 12, 2027, and the Bank takes into account industry comments to decide its supervisory strategy.

title: Jupiter Lend Halts Withdrawals Amid $6.3B Binance Hack Fears Despite Zero Exposure
summary:
Key Takeaways: Following the liquidity crisis due to market turmoil after Binance’s security breach of $6.3 billion, Jupiter Lend has temporarily shut down withdrawals. The protocol claims it never had
The post Jupiter Lend Halts Withdrawals Amid $6.3B Binance Hack Fears Despite Zero Exposure appear...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Following the liquidity crisis due to market turmoil after Binance’s security breach of $6.3 billion, Jupiter Lend has temporarily shut down withdrawals.
  • The protocol claims it never had any exposure to Binance, there have been no funds on the exchange, no loss of funds to report.
  • Withdrawals are likely to begin once loans are repaid and new supplies are available.

Uncertainty about the security issue on Binance has been seeping into the crypto sector and dragging down Jupiter Lend. According to the Solana lending platform, its infrastructure is live, but users will have to wait for the withdrawal of liquidity.

Read More: Binance Says $6.3B Hit in Security Breach, $3B Frozen After DevOps Laptop Compromise

  • Jupiter Lend Faces Liquidity Crunch
  • Why Are Withdrawals Being Delayed?
    • USDC Withdrawable Balance Raises Concerns

Jupiter Lend Faces Liquidity Crunch

On October 30, Jupiter addressed withdrawal delays through its official X account, explaining that broader market conditions had created a liquidity shortage across its lending pools.

Due to broader market conditions, there is currently a liquidity crunch impacting withdrawals.

Market conditions will cause users to deposit or repay their loans. As they do so, withdrawals will be able to process again.

This is normal and expected during events like today’s. Liquidity will soon be available again.

The protocol is functioning as expected and all funds are safe.

— Jupiter Earn (@jupiter_earn) October 30, 2026

Withdrawals would be resumed as market players deposit their assets or repay their loans, the protocol said. It said the situation was normal at all times of significant market volatility and all funds belonging to users are safe.

The announcement came amid increasing security fears surrounding Binance and market actions by the broader crypto sector. Jupiter had earlier said that it was keeping an eye on development and had never had any direct exposure to Binance.

Users asked how there could be any contradiction between the earlier reassurance and the delays in withdrawal, to which Jupiter responded that both the things were correct.

It noted that Binance couldn’t raise any money and the protocol didn’t lose any. The withdrawal pressure is not directly related to the exchange incident, the team said and instead is an indicator of reactions from the wider market.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

Why Are Withdrawals Being Delayed?

Jupiter Lend gifts work by means of lending pools where a deposited good can be borrowed by items like Borrow and Multiply. This is because not all deposits will be available immediately as some assets may be used to make loans on the go.

Liquidity may not keep up with the demand for it in periods of heavy withdrawal demand. The repayment of borrowers and fresh money for deposits are therefore significant in restoring withdrawal capacity.

USDC Withdrawable Balance Raises Concerns

Jupiter’s API data aptly pointed to the magnitude of the liquidity situation. Around 418.5 million USDCs in Earn deposit claims, with accrued interest, were visible at 7.14 a.m. ET, whereas 3.35 USDCs were immediately available to withdraw.

This difference reflects the amount of the claims of depositors serviceable by the bank at a given time versus the liquid funds held by the bank. That is not, however, a finding of loan impairment nor a determination that depositors have been losing money on the underlying loans.

In addition to the above, Jupiter documents further withdrawals based on available amounts and permission to withdraw. Users might have to make smaller withdrawals or wait for returns of liquidity.

The withdrawal scenario comes amidst worries over Binance’s security breach, estimated to cause around $6.3 billion damage to Binance.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • In Q3, Tether achieved an operating profit of $1.5 billion.
  • Reserve assets rose to almost $8 billion.
  • U.S. Treasury exposure reached $132.4 billion.

Tether also added another $1.5 billion in operating profits during the quarter, and considerably boosted the buffer for USDT. As of the end of September, the stablecoin issuer’s most recent BDO attestation reports $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities within total reserves.

Read More: Tether Backs Peso to Expand USDT Payments Across 4 Major Latin American Markets

  • Tether Reserve Buffer Jumps $3.8B in One Quarter
  • Treasury Holdings Drive Tether’s Earnings
    • Nine-Month Operating Profit Reaches $4.5B
    • USDT Still Controls More Than 60% of Stablecoins

Tether Reserve Buffer Jumps $3.8B in One Quarter

Tether’s surpluses surged from $4.1 billion at the end of June to $7.95 billion.

The increase added roughly $3.8 billion to the company’s reserve surplus in a single quarter. Total assets increased to $191.45 billion with total liabilities reaching $183.50 billion, with a majority of the liabilities held by digital tokens issued being about $183.47 billion.

USDT issuance demonstrated overall strength at approximately $184 billion despite fluctuations in market sentiment for cryptocurrencies during the first nine months of 2026.

Treasury Holdings Drive Tether’s Earnings

Tether said U.S. Treasury bills and reverse re-purchase agreements continued to be the primary sources of operating income. As of September 30 government debt represented the primary asset of the reserve portfolio exceeding $132.4 billion via direct and indirect holdings of Treasury bills.

That asset allocation will give them significant short-term liquidity, in short-term, liquid bonds, that can support redeeming when the market is in a state of stress.

Nine-Month Operating Profit Reaches $4.5B

Tether generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first three quarters of 2026.

Q3’s operating profit was reported at $1.5 billion, on par with in Q2. Tether said it had $4.11 billion in reserve for the second quarter, and that number grew dramatically for Q3.

The higher surplus provides Tether with more liquidity to redeem tokens and cover the cost of maintaining infrastructure during tough market conditions, CEO Paolo Ardoino wrote.

The statistics were revealed after Tether underwent its first full independent financial statement audit in August. KPMG U.S. gave an unqualified opinion for the company’s 2025 financial statements.

Read More: Tether Clears First-Ever KPMG Audit, Revealing a $6.8B Cushion for Crypto Markets

USDT Still Controls More Than 60% of Stablecoins

Despite the USDT circulating market capitalization dropping below the $184 billion USDT issuance figure reported in the quarter-end statement, USDT remains the largest dollar-backed token.

DefiLlama revealed that USDT netted a market capitalization of approximately USD 180 billion on 30 October, with the overall market of stablecoins valued at nearly USD 297 billion. This means the USDT is around 60.6% dominant.

The gap indicates the difference between Tether’s September 30 reporting date and the current market data at a point in time circulating.

As excess reserves near $8 billion and the portfolio is heavily weighted with Bitcoin securities, Tether will go into 2026’s 4th quarter with a considerably healthier financial cushion to support the crypto market’s most prominent stable coin.

title: Hoskinson Flags ‘Dangerous’ EIP-7702 Code After Binance’s $6.3B Crypto Breach
summary:
Key Takeaways: Hoskinson issued a warning about “seriously dangerous code” that is associated with the Binance hack. Based on an engineering researcher’s estimate, 50 EIP-7702 authorizations were directed at Binance
The post Hoskinson Flags ‘Dangerous’ EIP-7702 Code After Binance’s $6.3B Crypto Brea...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Hoskinson issued a warning about “seriously dangerous code” that is associated with the Binance hack.
  • Based on an engineering researcher’s estimate, 50 EIP-7702 authorizations were directed at Binance 14.
  • Even for EIP-7702, the account in question must still be properly cryptographically authorized.

Cardano’s founder Charles Hoskinson has echoed worries regarding Ethereum’s EIP-7702, following the investigators’ new allegation that the delegation function could be responsible for part of the massive Binance security breach.

The exchange has lost about $6.3 billion worth of crypto, based on recent reporting, but inquiries into the exact how the attackers obtained signing access continues.

  • Hoskinson Sounds Alarm Over Binance Sweeper Code
  • $823M USDC Vault Was Allegedly Within Reach
    • EIP-7702 Could Speed Execution, but It Cannot Forge Permission
    • Ethereum Specification Already Warns of Delegation Risk

Hoskinson Sounds Alarm Over Binance Sweeper Code

Hoskinson shared a technical breakdown from researcher CyberSatoshi with a blunt warning: “Careful, there is some seriously dangerous code out there.”

Careful, there is some seriously dangerous code out there. https://t.co/w7wM1nn0Lz

— Charles Hoskinson (@IOHK_Charles) October 30, 2026

The Binance wallet known as “Binance 14” was the target of a custom sweeper contract, the analysis states. When guiding the change of the wallet’s own ETH, it allegedly left precisely one ETH behind, which possibly meant that automated transaction systems continued to function as assets were taken away.

The contract also included a design that would continue to execute tokens even if their individual transfers were attempted to be failed.

Read More: Binance $5.5B Hack Exposed: 50 EIP-7702 Nonces Opened One Hot Wallet in Minutes

$823M USDC Vault Was Allegedly Within Reach

CyberSatoshi also stated that the wallet’s compromised execution function enabled it to act on an external vault that held some $823 million in USDC.

Reading the reconstructed bytecode of the Binance EIP-7702 sweeper (`0x63e8…6fae`) is wild.

This wasn’t a generic drainer. It was custom-engineered for Binance 14’s architecture:

– Leaves exactly 1 ether behind (`bal – 1 ether`) when sweeping ETH so Binance’s automated hot wallet queue wouldn’t error on gas and trip alarms.
– Uses raw `staticcall` + `continue` loops with custom error codes (`SweepItemFailed`) so one bricked or blacklisted ERC-20 wouldn’t revert the $6B batch.
– Includes a custom `callExecute` function to impersonate Binance 14 as controller of an external vault holding $823M in USDC.

They leave a comment: “robberies could be prevented if getaway cars were slower.”

You can’t fully blame EIP-7702, but it sped up the attack. Without 7702, draining 64 tokens plus an external $823M vault from a live exchange hot wallet meant fighting moving nonces across 70+ transactions. Defense systems would’ve killed it after tx #3.

With 7702, Lazarus sprayed 50 consecutive nonces in one type-4 payload, turned an EOA into a custom proxy, and atomically swept billions in a single block.

Ethereum core devs built the ultimate getaway car. Surgical state-sponsored engineering.

This could be etched onchain:
`if (bal > 1 ether) { https://t.co/ou2j9VqGvv{value: bal – 1 ether}(“”); }`

— CyberSatoshi 𓆙 (@XBToshi) October 30, 2026

Binance 14 supposedly knew more about that vault and delegated code can act on the basis of that wallet’s already granted just one activity.

They are presented based on researcher’s reconstruction and may not be reliable as Binance has confirmed. However, independent charges have reported seeing an EIP-7702 transaction that has 50 authorizations to be signed by Binance 14.

EIP-7702 Could Speed Execution, but It Cannot Forge Permission

The difference makes a lot of difference. EIP-7702 enables an EO A (Ethernet globally owned account) to delegate execution to the code of a smart contract. An authorization has a chain ID, an address of a delegate and a nonce and a signature. Ethereum checks out the signature prior to delegation.

This will prevent attackers from easily hijacking an arbitrary Binance wallet and loading malicious code on it. Cyber Satoshi’s team also noted that the criminal would have to obtain the private keys or have access to Binance’s signing systems which would be strong enough.

Delegated code, however, when granted access, can be made much more powerful on execution, as the code is executed within the context of the account.

Read More: Binance Says $6.3B Hit in Security Breach, $3B Frozen After DevOps Laptop Compromise

Ethereum Specification Already Warns of Delegation Risk

EIP-7702, officially written documentation of Ethereum, has a strong disclaimer that delegated code is available to full access of the account and should be carefully audited. The specification also relates to the fact that if the contracts of the delegates are not carefully crafted, the malicious party can essentially control the signer’s EOA with very few limitations.

The Binance incident of course gives rise to two distinct security concerns: firstly, how the attackers were able to acquire a valid signing key, and secondly, how it affected the speed and volume of asset transfers after the key was acquired.

Hoskinson’s message stresses the second point and the others are also the crux of uncovering the cause of the breach.

title: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance’s hot wallets were hacked for approximately $6.3 billion. Already, about $3 billion of assets have been seized. Binance allocated over $6.34 billion of reserves for user losses.
The post Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen appeared firs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance’s hot wallets were hacked for approximately $6.3 billion.
  • Already, about $3 billion of assets have been seized.
  • Binance allocated over $6.34 billion of reserves for user losses.

U.S. law enforcement has also been involved in the response to Binance’s massive crypto hack, working with the exchange and industry partners to track the sources of stolen funds. Binance says users will not absorb the losses and has committed company resources and its SAFU fund to make affected balances whole.

  • FBI Joins Hunt After Binance Loses $6.3 Billion
  • Nearly Half the Stolen Assets Are Already Frozen
    • Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Protect Users
    • Withdrawals and Proof of Reserves Take Center Stage

FBI Joins Hunt After Binance Loses $6.3 Billion

According to Binance, the hack caused about $6.3 billion worth of withdrawals from Binance hot wallets on Oct. 29. The FBI told Reuters it’s collaborating with both public and private partners to determine the extent of the situation and carry out investigative measures. According to Bloomberg separately Thursday, U.S. Secret Service investigators are also helping in the recovery.

Binance initially blamed the attack on a hacked DevOps engineer’s laptop but stated that they had found more points of attack. There is no evidence of the private keys in wallets being leaked, the company said.

Read More: Binance Says $6.3B Hit in Security Breach, $3B Frozen After DevOps Laptop Compromise

Nearly Half the Stolen Assets Are Already Frozen

Binance says approximately $3 billion of the affected assets has been frozen onchain through cooperation with token issuers, exchanges, blockchain intelligence firms and law enforcement. That leaves a lot of remaining victims not yet found and going unrecovered.

According to Reuters, the stablecoin issuers managed to freeze some of the stolen money, while assets like Bitcoin and Ether are less easily held due to the absence of centralized issuers that allow the assets to be frozen.

Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Protect Users

The incident is covered by over $6.34 billion of Binance’s company funds.

Of this total, roughly $5 billion is already locked in stolen tokens, which include BTC, ETH, BNB, USD, USDT, holding nickname assets. The exchange claims it is buying up the balance using market and OTC channels to interface with users.

According to Binance, around 80% of the value of those impacted is already covered by the $5 billion standing of reserves.

https://t.co/eeLPCUjIxR

— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026

The company stressed that the figures do not include assets that have already been frozen or otherwise protected, which remain subject to recovery and verification.

Withdrawals and Proof of Reserves Take Center Stage

The withdrawal process was temporarily paused, as Binance implements further security testing and remediation measures.

The exchange said it’s going to reopen withdrawals in steps as those checks are finished. It also plans to release a revamped PoR to allow users to check platform balances against customer balances.

An in-depth technical forensic analysis will also be undertaken after investigators determine the attack sequence.

The attack is now the biggest crypto-theft by value that has ever occurred on an exchange, calling for centralized exchanges to reinforce their transaction-signing infrastructure, hot wallet controls and real-time monitoring.

title: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen
summary: Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.
content:
Attackers behind Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion hack still control billions of dollars in stolen cryptocurrency despite efforts by token issuers to freeze the proceeds.

The attack, the largest in crypto history, began at 8:04 pm UTC Thursday and the perpetrators, linked to the same North Korean hackers behind last month’s Bitget hack, immediately began converting assets.

The game plan for the hackers was to convert the assets that could be frozen, like USDT and USDC, into ones that could not, such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH).

CertiK engineer Dickson Wu traced $500 million in USDT that was sent to one address, with $325 million sold to market makers for ETH by 20:59 UTC, less than an hour after the hack began.

They were racing against some of crypto’s most powerful gatekeepers: stablecoin giants like Tether and Circle, who had already begun blacklisting addresses associated with the theft.

Binance said Friday that about $3 billion of the stolen assets were frozen onchain out of an estimated $6.3 billion total, and that it is working with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain analytics firms to trace additional funds.

The scale of the theft is mind-boggling, even in crypto terms, but with around half of the assets already frozen, how much of the stolen crypto can the perpetrators actually spend?

Crypto with an off switch

Unlike BTC or ETH, which are decentralized cryptocurrencies with no central issuer and no one to hit the pause button, centralized stablecoins like Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC have issuers that can freeze tokens held at specific addresses.

Binance said it is working with law enforcement to trace the funds. Source: Binance

That gives them the power to act swiftly in incidents like these. Tether froze around $1.567 billion in USDT in total, with the first major freeze happening just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the attacker’s main Ethereum wallet.

Related: Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Circle froze around $823 million in USDC three minutes later, with other issuers like Ripple and World Liberty Financial following soon after.

The ability to immobilize crypto is not exclusively a stablecoin feature, and despite not having central issuers, some decentralized protocols like Arbitrum did not sit idly by.

Arbitrum’s Security Council moved around $30.5 million in ARB and ETH into an intermediary frozen wallet, where they can only be moved after further action by the council or a vote by Arbitrum DAO governance.

One important distinction remains — frozen funds don’t necessarily equate to recovered funds. Immobilizing assets prevents the suspected attackers from spending them, but it doesn’t automatically return them to Binance or its users.

The Aave complication

Decentralized lending protocol Aave adds another layer of complexity to the equation. Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, a wallet associated with the attackers deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave V3 on Ethereum and borrowed $44.6 million of wrapped Ether (WETH), around 40 minutes before the first freeze.

LlamaRisk, an Aave risk service provider, said in its 1:00 am update that the attacker’s position subsequently held around $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt. Aave said the position remained overcollateralized and did not put protocol suppliers at risk.

Largest crypto heists of all time. Source: Elliptic

Since the USDT had already been deposited into Aave’s lending pool, blacklisting the attacker’s wallet could not automatically retrieve the collateral held by the protocol, as Aave Chan Initiative founder Marc Zeller explained:

“USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol.”

To prevent further deposits and borrowing, Aave temporarily froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments, although existing users could still withdraw funds, repay loans and liquidate positions.

Aave later lifted its precautionary freeze across V3 and V4 markets, saying its contracts were unaffected and positions remained overcollateralized.

“Just another day in crypto,” Zeller said.

So what can the attackers actually keep?

Elliptic estimated that $2.84 billion had been frozen by 7:00 am UTC on Friday, while the attackers still controlled around $3.33 billion in assets that issuers could not immobilize.

And while the freeze almost halved the attackers’ profit pool, that doesn’t mean all the remaining funds are safe to recover.

Bitcoin and Ether don’t have a centralized token issuer that can blacklist individual addresses like Tether or Circle. So once stolen assets are converted into these native cryptocurrencies, transactions can be restricted, but freezing them is a lot harder.

Binance has pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, and says user assets remain safe; according to the latest update from Binance chief executive Richard Teng, the exchange is already “recovering stolen assets for users.”
